sections.label: Your Game's Unique Content
sections.note: Use this section to document what makes your game unique. List your specific mechanics, content scope, characters, and narrative elements. This section informs your risk assessment and vertical slice selection. Items here are freeform — the system will not generate tasks from this section automatically in v1.

subsections.label: Core Gameplay Mechanics
subsections.description: List the primary mechanics that define how your game plays. Each will be assessed for risk and mapped to milestones.

subsections.label: Content Inventory
subsections.description: List all content that must ship in v1.0: levels, stages, scenes, areas, missions, maps, chapters, etc.

subsections.label: Characters & Entities
subsections.description: List player characters, NPCs, enemies, and other significant entities in scope for v1.0.

subsections.label: Items, Collectibles & Unlockables
subsections.description: List items, weapons, abilities, collectibles, power-ups, and unlockables in scope for v1.0.

subsections.label: Story & Narrative Elements
subsections.description: List story beats, dialogue exchanges, cutscenes, lore, and narrative elements in scope for v1.0.

items.description: Primary game mechanic functions as designed under all normal conditions
Input is responsive and consistent across all control schemes
No soft-lock or progression-blocking states reachable through normal play
Core loop is playable without external guidance
Failure state and retry loop work correctly and return to a valid game state
Game rules and win/loss conditions are communicated clearly to the player
All secondary mechanics integrate with the primary mechanic without conflict or unintended interaction
Difficulty curve validated with external playtesters — no unintended difficulty spikes or dead zones
Core movement and actions feel good — juice, weight, and responsiveness match the intended design
Edge-case inputs tested: rapid presses, held inputs, simultaneous multi-key/button inputs, diagonal movement
Engine/publisher logo displays correctly (if required by license)
Logo sequences are skippable after minimum required display time
Initial load completes within target time on minimum spec hardware
No missing assets or placeholder content visible at launch
Level loading is async with a visible progress indicator
Graceful handling of load failures — clear error message, no silent hang
First-run experience tested on a completely clean machine — no dependency on prior settings or files
Config / settings file created correctly on first launch in the expected platform-appropriate location

sections.label: First-Time User Experience (FTUE)
sections.note: FTUE covers everything a brand-new player encounters from the moment they launch the game for the first time through their first meaningful gameplay moment. These items are distinct from tutorial content — FTUE is about friction, trust, and first impressions, not mechanic instruction. Test this section exclusively on people who have never seen the game before.

items.description: Time from launch to first meaningful player input is within target — new players are not stuck watching unskippable sequences before they can act
No wall-of-text rules explanation before the player has had a chance to touch the game — information is introduced through play, not upfront reading
First 5–10 minutes tested specifically with first-time players — their experience observed and documented, not assumed
The first thing the player is asked to do (move, click, select) is unambiguous — no new player has been observed ignoring or missing it
Complex systems (inventory, skill trees, crafting) are not surfaced until the player has a foothold in the core loop — no overwhelming menus on session one
Default settings (volume, resolution, controls) produce a good experience out of the box — new players should not need to visit settings before enjoying the game
Controller is detected and prompts switch automatically on first launch — a player who plugs in a gamepad before starting sees gamepad glyphs immediately
Character name input and character creation flow are clear, skippable or have sensible defaults, and cannot be entered in a broken state (if applicable)
Difficulty selection (if present at start) gives enough context for a new player to make an informed choice — descriptions reflect actual gameplay impact, not vague labels
A save file is created or a checkpoint is reached before any sequence a new player might find confusing or want to replay — no loss of progress from early quit
Any FTUE-specific sequences, cinematics, or locked menus are skippable or bypassed on subsequent playthroughs — returning players are not re-onboarded
Player is not required to configure keybindings, create an account, or accept lengthy legal screens before experiencing the game's hook
The core fantasy or emotional hook of the game is delivered within the first session — a new player can articulate what the game is about after 10–15 minutes
The game's first designed outcome for the player is a success, not a failure — new players experience competence before they experience challenge
Audio is on and at a reasonable level by default — new players do not launch to silence and wonder if something is broken
FTUE sequence is crash-free across all tested hardware configurations — a crash in the first 10 minutes is a near-certain refund
Game logo and title art display correctly
Press to start / any key prompt functions correctly (if applicable)
Version number displayed somewhere accessible (main menu or settings screen)
Background music and visuals loop correctly without interruption or seam
New Game / Start functions correctly and consistently
Continue / Load Game functions correctly
Options / Settings accessible from the main menu
Credits screen accessible from the main menu
Quit with confirmation dialog on all target platforms
All menu items fully navigable with keyboard, mouse, and gamepad — no dead-end focus states
Menu music stops or transitions cleanly when entering gameplay — no audio bleed

Attract loop plays automatically after a defined idle period on the title screen, cycles through gameplay or demo footage, and exits cleanly back to the title screen on any input — with no side effects on game state or audio (applicable to arcade, kiosk, trade show, and living-room console builds; delete for PC/mobile-only releases)
Pause menu accessible in all active game states (Resume, Restart, Options, Quit)
Pause completely freezes gameplay and audio (or pauses intentionally per design)
Autosave occurs at checkpoints or intervals with a visible indicator
Save-on-quit behavior is defined, implemented, and communicated to the player
Manual save option available if appropriate for the game's genre (if applicable)
Save file corruption not reproducible under normal or abnormal conditions
Continue from save returns player to the correct game state
Cloud save conflict resolution handled gracefully (if applicable)
Save files stored in platform-appropriate location
Pause cannot be used to exploit timing windows, dodge unavoidable damage, or bypass intended challenge
Save slot UI shows useful metadata — timestamp, play time, level/chapter reached (if applicable)
Save file versioning handled — older saves load or are migrated gracefully after game updates (if applicable)
Master volume control works and persists across sessions
Music volume is independent of SFX volume and persists
SFX volume control works and persists
Resolution options available and apply correctly on all target platforms
Windowed / fullscreen toggle works on all target platforms
VSync toggle available and functional
Brightness / gamma adjustment available
Motion blur toggle available (if applicable)
UI / HUD scale adjustment available (if applicable)
Key rebinding available for keyboard controls
Full controller support on all target platforms
Input hints update automatically to match active input device
Language / locale selector available (if supporting multiple languages)
Voice/dialogue volume control separate from SFX and persists (if voice acted)
Frame rate cap option available (30 / 60 / 120 / Unlimited) for players with thermal or battery concerns
Camera shake toggle or intensity slider available
Controller button rebinding available (if applicable)
Reset-to-defaults option available in settings — does not reset save progress
All settings persist correctly across sessions, restarts, and game updates

sections.label: Accessibility
sections.note: Mark items N/A only if they genuinely do not apply to your game. When in doubt, include — accessibility features help more players than you expect.

items.description: Subtitles or captions available and toggleable for all dialogue and key audio events (if applicable)
Subtitle font size and background contrast options available (if subtitles present)
Colorblind mode or alternative color palette available for any color-critical gameplay element
Screen shake toggle or intensity slider available
Reduced motion option available — disables non-essential flashing and particle-heavy effects
High contrast UI option available for improved readability (if applicable)
Text size / UI scale option available for all player-visible text
Critical audio events have visual equivalents for players who may not hear them (if applicable)
Subtitle speaker names included for conversations with multiple characters (if applicable)
No uncontrolled rapid flashing exceeding 3Hz in any game state — or a prominent photosensitivity warning at launch
Aim assist option available for controller players in games requiring precise targeting (if applicable)
Timing assist or slow-motion option available for time-critical inputs (if applicable)
Difficulty settings or custom assist options available — no shame in supporting all player types
Game can be paused at any time during active play (not just at checkpoints)
HUD displays only essential information and updates correctly at all times
Resource counters accurate and update correctly in real time
Objective / quest tracker visible and accurate (if applicable)
No UI elements clipped, off-screen, or overlapping at any supported resolution
All interactive UI elements have consistent visual and/or audio feedback
Loading indicators present for any operation exceeding one second
Full keyboard + mouse support with discoverable bindings
Full gamepad support on all target platforms
Input device hot-swap detected and UI updates accordingly
Tutorial or onboarding flow complete and accurate (if applicable)
Tutorial skip option available on repeat play
In-game controls reference accessible at any time during play
UI respects safe area margins on all target platforms — nothing critical cut off on TVs or notched screens
Player always knows what happened — damage numbers, hit confirmation, state changes are communicated clearly
Death / game over screen communicates clearly what happened and what options the player has next
Map or minimap is accurate and updates in real time as the player explores (if applicable)
Inventory / item management UI is functional and readable at all supported resolutions (if applicable)
HUD can be toggled off for screenshot mode or player preference (if applicable)
No placeholder or missing audio in any shipping area of the game
No placeholder text or lorem ipsum visible to players
Audio mix is acceptable at default settings across all target platforms
No audio clipping at any volume level
Music loops without an audible seam or gap
All audio assets mixed at correct relative levels — SFX does not drown music, etc.
Dialogue system handles all content without errors or dead ends (if applicable)
All voiced lines have corresponding subtitle text (if voice acted)
3D/spatial audio sources attenuate correctly and are positioned accurately (if applicable)
Audio events do not stack or double-trigger under rapid or repeated player actions
Ambient / environmental audio present and appropriate in all shipping areas (if applicable)
High-frequency SFX (footsteps, shots, hits) use randomized variation to avoid listener fatigue

sections.label: Localization & Text Completeness
sections.note: Mark all items N/A if releasing in a single language with no localization plans. Even single-language releases should complete the first three items.

items.description: All player-visible strings are externalized — no hardcoded UI text in source code
No string truncation or text overflow at any supported resolution
Character encoding is UTF-8 throughout; special characters render correctly
All player-visible text proofread for spelling and grammar in the primary language
Numbers, dates, and currency display in locale-appropriate format (if multi-locale)
All strings translated and reviewed for each supported language (if applicable)
All fonts support the full character set for every target language — no missing glyphs
Right-to-left text layout supported for Arabic, Hebrew, or other RTL languages (if applicable)
UI layout accommodates text expansion for verbose languages (German, Finnish) without overflow
No placeholder art, grey-box geometry, or dev-only debug visuals visible in any shipping area
Art style is consistent throughout — no jarring mismatches in resolution, line weight, or palette
All characters and interactive objects have complete animation sets — no T-poses, frozen frames, or missing transitions
No player-visible geometry clipping — character limbs, weapons, or objects do not clip through walls or other entities
All VFX (hit sparks, explosions, magic, ambient particles) are complete and final
Lighting is consistent and intentional in all shipping areas — no unlit black zones or blown-out areas
All UI art, icons, and HUD elements are final — consistent style, correct resolution for target displays
Cutscenes and cinematics are final quality — correct aspect ratio, no visible seams or pops (if applicable)
Pixel art or texture assets render crisply at all supported resolutions — no unintended blurring or nearest-neighbor artifacts
Target frame rate maintained in all representative gameplay areas — tested under worst-case conditions
No gameplay-disrupting hitches or freezes during normal play
No persistent micro-stutter or frame pacing issues in gameplay areas
No detectable memory leaks during a normal play session — tested over extended play
Level / scene load times acceptable on minimum spec hardware — documented in system requirements
Performance verified on documented minimum specification hardware — not just development machines
VRAM usage within safe limits on minimum spec GPU — no out-of-memory crashes at min settings
CPU usage at acceptable levels on minimum spec hardware — no pegging single core to 100%
Game recovers gracefully from system sleep / suspend and resume on all target platforms
Alt-tab / window focus loss handled correctly — no crash, audio bleed, or broken state on return
Platform store integration working — entitlements, DLC hooks, cloud saves
Achievements / trophies trigger correctly and are not exploitable (if applicable)
Cloud save sync works correctly across devices (if applicable)
Target frame rate maintained in all representative gameplay areas
No detectable memory leaks during a normal play session
Unhandled exceptions do not crash to desktop silently — errors are caught or logged
Alt-tab / window focus loss handled correctly on all desktop target platforms
Minimum and maximum supported resolutions enforced and tested
Clean uninstall leaves no orphaned files in unexpected system locations
Build pipeline produces valid, testable builds consistently and reproducibly
All third-party license requirements met — fonts, audio, middleware, engine, libraries
Content rating certificate obtained (PEGI, ESRB, etc.) and applied to store page
Content descriptor warnings set correctly on all distribution platforms
Privacy policy accessible in-game or linked from store page if collecting any user data
EULA / Terms of Service link accessible if required by platform
In-game credits complete and accurate — development team, music, third-party licenses
All platform certification / submission requirements reviewed and satisfied (Steam, itch.io, console TRC/TCR)
Platform overlays (Steam, Discord, Xbox Game Bar) do not cause crashes or rendering issues
DRM integration verified — game launches and functions correctly on end-user machines (if DRM used)
Final build size within stated requirements and documented on the store page
Data collection and opt-out mechanisms comply with GDPR / CCPA if collecting user data (if applicable)

sections.label: Multiplayer & Online Features
sections.note: Delete this entire section if your game is single-player only with no online features.

items.description: Lobby creation, joining, and matchmaking work correctly under all expected conditions
Game session persists gracefully if one player disconnects — reconnect or graceful end handled
Host migration works without ending the session when the host disconnects (if peer-to-peer)
Gameplay is playable and fair at documented maximum supported latency
Anti-cheat or server-authoritative validation in place for competitive modes (if applicable)
Profanity filter or name validation in place for user-generated text (usernames, chat, etc.)
Report and mute functionality available for player-to-player interactions (if applicable)
Server region selection available where latency meaningfully impacts gameplay
Game launches and functions in offline mode for single-player content if network is unavailable (if applicable)
Network errors surface clear messages to the player — no silent failures or frozen states
Leaderboards display correctly, update in real time, and are protected from obvious exploits (if applicable)
No known critical bugs: crash, progression block, or data loss
Bug tolerance by severity documented: crash=0, blocker=0, major=max_n defined, minor=unlimited
No placeholder art or debug visuals visible in the final build
All player-visible text is spelled correctly
Performance targets verified on minimum specification hardware
No gameplay-disrupting hitches or freezes during normal play
No persistent micro-stutter or frame pacing issues in gameplay areas
No known game-breaking exploits or unintended progression bypasses
At least one external playtest completed with people unfamiliar with the game — findings documented and acted on
A complete playthrough from new game to credits completed without hitting any showstopper issues
Store page live with all required fields completed
Store tags and categories set correctly to maximize discoverability
Pricing set correctly and confirmed on all distribution platforms
Capsule / cover images finalized and meet platform specifications
Minimum 5 screenshots captured, finalized, and uploaded
Trailer published and linked on store page
System requirements listed accurately on store page (tested, not estimated)
Final build uploaded and validated on distribution platform
Press / review key distribution plan prepared and keys generated (if applicable)
Day-1 patch strategy documented; hotfix build pipeline verified
Launch announcement drafted and scheduled across all active channels
Store description is compelling, spell-checked, and free of lorem ipsum or placeholder text
Press kit prepared with logo, key art, screenshots, trailer link, fact sheet, and contact info
Influencer / content creator outreach plan prepared — targets identified, pitches drafted
Steam wishlist notification campaign ready — launch email will fire to wishlisted users automatically
Launch day social media posts drafted and scheduled across all active channels
Release date/time confirmed on all platforms — embargo lifted, store page set to publish on schedule
Fresh install test passes on a clean machine with no prior game files
All menu navigation paths tested and verified — no dead-ends
All settings tested, applied, and persist correctly across sessions
Save / load integrity confirmed across multiple cycles and edge cases
Controller disconnect and reconnect handled gracefully mid-game
Performance verified on documented minimum specification hardware
UI and gameplay tested at minimum and maximum supported resolutions
Alt-tab / window focus loss tested on all desktop target platforms
External playtest completed; sign-off recorded with key findings documented
Multiple simultaneously connected controllers do not cause input confusion (if applicable)
Ultrawide (21:9) and super-ultrawide (32:9) aspect ratios tested — no broken UI or gameplay (if supported)
System sleep and resume tested during active gameplay — no crash or corrupted state
Complete playthrough from new game to credits conducted on final build — no skipped sections
Regression test pass completed after all final fixes — no new issues introduced by last-minute changes
Crash reporting or exception logging integrated and verified — even minimal or opt-in
Hotfix build pipeline tested — a patch can be produced and deployed within 24 hours
Support or contact channel live and monitored — email, Discord, itch comments, etc.
Community response plan ready — how will you handle bug reports and reviews at launch?
Review solicitation plan in place — in-game prompt, follow-up email, or similar
FAQ or known issues page prepared for common launch-day questions
Sales, wishlists, and review monitoring set up — you will know within hours if something is wrong at launch
Post-launch content or patch roadmap communicated to players — sets expectations and builds goodwill

_meta.description: Comprehensive Definition of Done for Indie Game Developers. Designed for deletion — spend more time removing items that don't apply than adding new ones. Genre-specific sections contain only items unique to that genre; cross-genre items live in the main sections.
_meta.usage: Work through each section top-to-bottom. Mark items complete, N/A, or deferred. Delete entire sections or items that genuinely do not apply to your game. Add project-specific items where you find gaps.
